objections.headline: Things we get asked.

items.q: Our staff won't switch to a new system.
items.a: Your staff isn't switching to a new way of working – they're doing the same things they've always done: creating appointments, confirming them, marking them done. The difference is it's now tracked instead of remembered. Most front-desk staff are comfortable within a day.

items.q: We have too many bookings to migrate.
items.a: Starting fresh doesn't mean losing history. Existing appointments stay where they are. You start using the platform for new bookings, and the value is immediate – without a migration project.

items.q: We already tried booking software before. It didn't stick.
items.a: Most booking tools are built for customers – not for the operational reality of a multi-branch team with managers, therapists, and admins. This one is built for how your business actually runs: with roles, branches, status flows, and a chain of accountability.

items.q: We're not sure we need all of this.
items.a: You don't need to use everything on day one. Most businesses start with booking creation and status management – and that alone changes how the morning works. Everything else is there when you're ready.

objections.sub: Answers to what owners ask before they switch.

objections.headline: Things we get asked.

items.q: Our managers already walk the floor. Why do we need a dashboard?
items.a: Walking the floor tells you what's happening in the room you're standing in. It doesn't tell you what happened five minutes ago in the room you already left, or what's building up at another branch. The dashboard doesn't replace managing – it removes the guessing part of it.

items.q: Won't staff resist logging every status change?
items.a: They're not logging anything extra – they're tapping the same status change they'd normally just say out loud to a manager. It takes less time than the conversation it replaces, and it means they stop getting interrupted to give updates.

items.q: What actually stops staff from giving unauthorized discounts?
items.a: The system enforces the limit at the point of sale, not after the fact. If a staff member tries to go beyond what they're cleared for, it doesn't go through – it routes to a manager instead. There's no relying on someone remembering the policy.

items.q: We run multiple branches. Can one owner really see all of them at once?
items.a: Yes – that's the point of the consolidated view. Revenue, queue activity, and staff status across every branch sit on one dashboard, updated live. You're not waiting for each manager to send a summary at the end of the day.

objections.sub: Answers to what owners ask before they switch.

objections.headline: Things we get asked.

items.q: How do we know the numbers are actually accurate?
items.a: Every payment is tied to a specific booking, staff member, and timestamp – there's no free-text field to fudge. Once a day is locked, entries can't be edited, only reversed, and the reversal is visible in the trail.

items.q: What stops staff from pocketing cash?
items.a: Cash payments are recorded against the booking the moment they happen, and branch managers see the running total in real time – before the drawer is ever counted. A mismatch between what's recorded and what's counted shows up immediately, not at month-end.

items.q: We have years of records in Excel. What happens to them?
items.a: You keep them. Zenly doesn't need your history to work going forward – everything from your go-live date is captured automatically, and your old spreadsheets stay exactly where they are for reference.

items.q: This sounds like more steps for a busy front desk.
items.a: It's fewer. Recording a payment takes one screen – mode, amount, done. The close that used to take 45 minutes with a calculator now takes 30 seconds, because the totals were already correct all day.

items.q: Our business type is pretty niche. Does Zenly actually support it?
items.a: Zenly currently supports over ten distinct verticals out of the box, spanning spas, salons, dental clinics, and fitness studios. If your business sits close to one of these, onboarding takes a configuration change, not a rebuild. If it doesn't, we'll tell you plainly before you sign anything — we'd rather say no than force a bad fit.

items.q: We already have our own terminology. Will we have to adopt Zenly's instead?
items.a: No. The terminology is configured to match your business, not the other way around. 'Session' can stay 'Session' or become 'Appointment' — whatever your staff already says out loud is what shows up on screen.

items.q: This sounds like a custom setup. What does that cost us?
items.a: It isn't custom development — it's configuration, and it's included. Picking a vertical during onboarding maps existing terminology, fields, and service categories to your business. Nobody writes code, so there's no custom-build invoice waiting at the end.

items.q: How long before we're actually live with our own setup?
items.a: Most branches go from selecting a vertical to taking their first real booking in under an hour. There's no development queue to sit in — the configuration step is the entire onboarding process.

objections.headline: Things we get asked.

items.q: Will data leak between our branches?
items.a: No. Each branch's bookings, staff, and financials are stored separately by default. Cross-branch visibility exists for the roles that need it — owners and area managers — and it's a deliberate view, not a side effect of shared storage.

items.q: If branches run independently, don't we lose central visibility?
items.a: Independence at the branch level doesn't mean opacity at the top. Every branch feeds the same consolidated dashboard in real time — managers still run their own operations, but nothing they do is invisible to you.

items.q: Does this get expensive as we add more branches?
items.a: You're adding a branch record to an existing account, not standing up a new system. There's no separate infrastructure or per-location vendor contract to negotiate every time you open a location.

items.q: How long does onboarding a new branch actually take?
items.a: Under a day in practice — create the branch, add staff accounts scoped to it, set local pricing, and it's ready to take bookings. No technical work, no waiting on a vendor's setup team.

objections.sub: Answers to what owners ask before adding their next branch.
